title: About COVID-19

sections.heading: About COVID-19
sections.text: COVID-19 most often causes respiratory symptoms that can feel much like a cold, the flu, or pneumonia. COVID-19 may attack more than your lungs and respiratory system. Other parts of your body may also be affected by the disease. Most people with COVID-19 have mild symptoms, but some people become severely ill.

sections.heading: About COVID-19
sections.text: Some people, including those with minor or no symptoms, will develop Post-COVID Conditions – also called "Long COVID."

sections.heading: How COVID-19 spreads
sections.text: COVID-19 spreads when an infected person breathes out droplets and very small particles that contain the virus. Other people can breathe in these droplets and particles, or these droplets and particles can land on others' eyes, nose, or mouth. In some circumstances, these droplets may contaminate the surfaces they touch.

sections.heading: How COVID-19 spreads
sections.text: Anyone infected with COVID-19 can spread it, even if they do NOT have symptoms. COVID-19 can even spread from people to animals in some situations.

sections.text: Understanding your COVID-19 risk and the risks that might affect others can help you make decisions to protect yourself and others.

sections.heading: About variants
sections.text: Viruses are constantly changing, including the virus that causes COVID-19. These changes occur over time and can lead to the emergence of variants that may have new characteristics, including different ways of spreading. Slowing the spread of the virus, by protecting yourself and others, can help slow new variants from developing.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.text: There are many actions you can take to help protect you, your household, and your community from COVID-19. CDC's Respiratory Virus Guidance provides actions you can take to lower the risk of COVID-19 transmission (catching and spreading COVID-19) and lower the risk of severe illness if you get sick.
